Becoming a Machine Learning Engineer or ML Researcher in Singapore: A 2026 Market Report for a New NTU MS-in-AI

For a fresh MS in AI from NTU with prior SWE experience at Interactive Brokers and Credit Suisse plus RL/quant research, the Machine Learning Engineer (MLE) path is wide open and well-matched; pure Research Scientist roles in Singapore (A*STAR, big- tech labs, ByteDance's PhD "Global Frontier Tech" track) are largely gated behind a PhD with top-conference publications, so target Research Engineer / Applied Scientist roles instead of Research Scientist. Compensation for new-grad MLE roles in Singapore spans roughly S$5,000– S$10,000/month base depending on employer tier: AI-skilled junior software/ML engineers earn a median around S$6,000/month (NodeFlair 2026), while big-tech total- comp packages reach ~S$114K–S$200K/year (Levels.fyi: Google L3 ~S$121K, ByteDance entry ~S$114K–126K). Quant firms (Optiver, Jane Street, Jump, Citadel, IMC, HRT all have Singapore offices) pay the most but are the hardest to enter. The single highest-leverage move is to convert the SAC-Dirichlet RL / HMM regime- detection thesis into a polished, deployed, documented portfolio project (GitHub + MLOps stack) and to lead the resume with production engineering keywords (PyTorch, Docker/Kubernetes, cloud, LLMs/RAG) rather than presenting as a pure researcher — this directly addresses the market's dominant demand for production ML skills.

Hiring teams are answering "Why you, not anyone else?" because headcount is tight. 3. **New "scary" rounds** are the differentiator in 2026: (a) ML infra design (Netflix, Snap, Reddit, DoorDash, Notion), (b) multi-level OOP, (c) LLM/ML coding (implement Transformer encoders/decoders, LoRA, KV cache, beam search, autograd from scratch), (d) research presentations (job-talk style), and (e) AI-assisted coding (Meta's CoderPad round where you co-code with an LLM and are judged on how you direct/verify it). 4. **Three role categories need genuinely different preparation.** Product MLE ≈ coding + ML system design + ML fundamentals + behavioural. **Levels — new grad vs mid-level:** - *New grad / early career:* online assessments matter more; ML fundamentals and coding fluency are decisive; graduate programmes (DBS MA, OCBC GTP, AIAP) and campus hiring are the main doors; portfolio and internships substitute for work history. - *Mid-level (with startup background):* project deep dives and domain fit become the deciding factor; expect ML/infra system design and stronger behavioural/leadership signals; your startup story (end-to-end ownership, shipping under constraints, scrappiness) is an asset — frame it around measurable impact and technical depth.

**Coding (LeetCode).** Work NeetCode's beginner + advanced courses, then NeetCode 250; do timed LeetCode weekly contests for Google-style hards. Focus on problem-solving intuition over memorising company tags. Connect problems to scalable data-processing patterns (sliding window, heaps/top-k, tries/inverted index, union-find). Target: 1 Easy+1 Medium or 2 Mediums in 45 min (Meta), or 1 Hard with follow-ups in 45 min (Google/Snap).

Implement architectures from scratch (MLP, CNN, RNN/LSTM/GRU, Transformer encoder/decoder) and building blocks (layer norm, causal/bidirectional attention, residuals, optimizers). Reproduce Sebastian Raschka's "Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)" and Karpathy's GPT-2 video / nanoGPT / micrograd. Know Flash Attention, LoRA, beam search, KV cache.
